title: Client Stability Handbook: Opinionated retry presets and de-duplication key semantics
creator: Priya Sharma
description:
Problem statement: SDK consumers across Python, TypeScript, and Go need consistent, safe defaults for retries and de-duplication that balance cost, latency, and correctness. Current client libraries diverge in default backoff curves, retryable error classification, and idempotency key generation, causing production surprises and inconsistent behavior when customers swap languages.

Goal: Produce an opinionated, implementable handbook and default library primitives that: (1) define 3 sensible retry profiles, (2) standardize idempotency/de-duplication key semantics across sync and streaming flows, (3) provide a clear retryable-error taxonomy, and (4) ship canonical examples for Python/TS/Go SDKs. The handbook will be the source-of-truth for cross-SDK implementation and for SDK docs and quickstarts.
acceptance_criteria: A concise handbook document exists and is approved by SDK leads (Python/TS/Go) and Runtime reliability lead.
Three retry profiles (conservative | latency-optimized | throughput-optimized) are specified with numeric defaults for initial_delay, max_delay, multiplier, max_attempts, and jitter strategy.
A single idempotency key contract is defined that covers one-off requests, multi-chunk uploads, and streaming append/resume semantics.
A retryable-error taxonomy is published with example HTTP/gRPC codes and recommended handling (immediate retry, exponential backoff, do-not-retry).
Prototype helper primitives (RetryPolicy, IdempotencyKey, StreamCheckpoint) are implemented in each SDK with matching semantics and unit tests.
Examples for common patterns (single-shot generation, long-polling, streaming chunked uploads, resumable chat streams) included in SDK docs.
Feature flagged rollout plan exists for gated release to beta customers and internal dogfooding teams.
Telemetry hooks include attempt_count, last_error_category, and dedup_key in traces for postmortems.
Backward-compatible opt-outs available so customers can retain previous behavior.
Release notes and migration guide prepared for SDK consumers.
technical_design:
Overview:
- Provide a small set of opinionated RetryProfile objects with numeric defaults. Avoid one-size-fits-all.
- Standardize a de-dup (idempotency) key format: <client-prefix>:<unix-ms>:<operation-hash> with optional user-provided token. SDKs will expose a generator helper that respects user-provided keys and validates format.
- Streaming: use small checkpoint records (stream offset + last-token-hash + timestamp) that are resumable server-side; SDKs include StreamCheckpoint helpers and automatic checkpoint persistence hooks.
- Telemetry: emit structured attributes: retry.profile, retry.attempts, retry.last_error_category, dedup.key.present, stream.checkpointed.

Retry profiles (proposal):
1) conservative — initial_delay=200ms, multiplier=2.0, max_delay=3s, max_attempts=5, jitter=full
2) latency-optimized — initial_delay=100ms, multiplier=1.6, max_delay=750ms, max_attempts=4, jitter=equal
3) throughput-optimized — initial_delay=500ms, multiplier=2.5, max_delay=8s, max_attempts=8, jitter=full
(Exact numbers are chosen to balance token-cost and tail-latency; see bench notes in links.)

Idempotency/de-dup semantics:
- One-shot requests: server dedup window = 5 minutes by default. SDK will set header X-Redwood-Idempotency unless user-supplies header. SDK-generated keys include high-entropy nonce.
- Chunked uploads: each chunk includes dedup key derived from upload-id + chunk-index; server dedup window matches upload lifecycle.
- Streams: SDK persists StreamCheckpoint locally (in-memory + optional disk hook) and attaches checkpoint token for resume. Checkpoint TTL = 1 hour by default.

Retryable-error taxonomy (category -> handling):
- TRANSIENT_NETWORK (tcp resets, connection refused, DNS) -> retry with profile
- RATE_LIMIT (HTTP 429 / gRPC ResourceExhausted) -> retry with backoff and respect Retry-After header if present
- MODEL_OVERLOAD (503 with model-signal or custom header) -> retry with throughput-optimized profile as fallback to cheaper variant; consider circuit-breaker to avoid spin
- SERVER_ERROR (5xx not classified) -> conservative retry, then surface to caller
- CLIENT_BAD_REQUEST (4xx) -> do not retry (user fix required)
- STREAM_EOS_MISMATCH (streaming checksum/seq mismatch) -> do-not-retry; surface for manual reconciliation

SDK API surface (high level):
- RetryPolicy object: fields for initial_delay_ms, multiplier, max_delay_ms, max_attempts, jitter_kind, should_retry(error) -> boolean
- IdempotencyKey helper: generate(operation_name, user_token_opt) -> string; validate(key) -> boolean
- StreamCheckpoint: save() -> token, restore(token) -> state, ttl_ms configurable

Compatibility & migration: defaults shipped behind minor-version feature flag. Old SDK behavior preserved via opt-out flag in client constructor.
examples:
Python single-shot example:
from redwood import Client, RetryPolicy, IdempotencyKey
client = Client(retry_policy=RetryPolicy.profile('conservative'))
key = IdempotencyKey.generate('generate-text', user_token=None)
resp = client.generate(prompt='Hello', idempotency_key=key)
rollout_plan: 1) Merge handbook and SDK prototypes behind feature flag in each repo. 2) Internal dogfooding: enable for Redwood Console and internal CLI. 3) Beta program: opt-in customers (<=20) for 2 weeks. 4) Monitor telemetry (attempt_count, last_error_category, dedup_key_present) and rollback-if-error-rate-increases > 3x. 5) Gradual 100% rollout after 2 stable weeks and signoff from reliability and SDK leads.
risks_mitigation:
Risk: Defaults may increase cost for high-throughput customers. Mitigation: provide throughput-optimized profile and easy opt-out; include cost-sensitivity guidance in docs.
Risk: Server-side dedup window mismatch with client expectations. Mitigation: coordinate with server runtime owners to publish dedup windows via discovery endpoint and server response headers.
Risk: Streaming resume token leakage. Mitigation: tokens are opaque, short TTL, and include HMAC signed by server when enabled.
Risk: Edge-case errors misclassified as retryable. Mitigation: telemetry + conservative default; add an override hook should_retry(error) for advanced customers.
